options.text: Air pressure outside the straw is greater than the pressure inside her mouth, so outside air pushes the juice up the straw.
Air pressure inside her mouth is greater than outside, so the juice is pushed up from inside the straw.
The juice rises even when the air pressure outside equals the air pressure inside her mouth.
Atmospheric air around the glass pulls the juice up the straw with no pressure difference needed.

stem:
Leela drinks mango juice through a straw. She lowers the air pressure inside her mouth while the straw dips into the juice.

Why does the juice rise in the straw?

teacher.key_rationale: Lower pressure in the mouth creates a pressure difference; higher outside atmospheric pressure pushes the juice up the straw.
